samples.summary: The only gate that refuses a share-link viewer's write is disabled by default (shadow mode fails open); this change adds a warning log but leaves the bypass in place
samples.evidence: `handleAuth` computes a correct deny (`hasAccess` → `link.role === 'editor'` for `needWrite`) and then discards it: with `this.enforce` false (line 116, the default — no deployment config in the repo sets `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE`, and `packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:185` documents `false` as the default) it returns `{allowed: true}` at line 163. Attack: open a viewer-role share link, POST the share token to `/auth/yorkie-token/share` (auth.controller.ts:82 — public, no role check by design), read `VITE_YORKIE_PUBLIC_KEY` out of the bundle, attach a bare Yorkie SDK client to `note-<documentId>` and PushPull writes. Every client-side guard added by this change (`readOnlyNoteStore`, `EditorState.readOnly`, the `changeFilter`) is irrelevant to that client. The diff's own docs say exactly this. This is pre-existing, deliberate rollout behaviour and the change only makes it observable (`logPosture`), so a verifier may classify it as accepted design — but as shipped, viewer-role share links are write-capable, so I am reporting it rather than silently accepting it.

samples.summary: New Risks bullet credits revision history with asserting `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true` itself; no such runtime assertion exists
samples.evidence: The mitigation text reads "features whose safety depends on the distinction (the public template tier, revision history) assert `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true` themselves rather than assuming it". True for the template tier (`register-templates.ts:154`, `template-review.ts:80`, `template.service.ts:470`). For revision history there is no backend module at all (`packages/backend/src/**/*revision*` matches nothing) and the only occurrence of the flag is a test setting the env var (`packages/backend/test/revision-history.e2e-spec.ts:292`); `packages/frontend/README.md:33-41` states outright that version history has *no* client gate and that on a shadow-mode deployment "any attached client can read and restore every past snapshot". A security doc crediting a safeguard the code lacks invites an operator to enable the feature on a shadow-mode install and expose full document history (including pre-share content) to anonymous viewers.
searchedFor: read packages/frontend/README.md around the version-history note

samples.summary: Newly-wired notes share upload sends the bearer share token in a URL query string, contradicting the repo's own decision to keep it out of URLs and access logs
samples.evidence: `shareTokenImageUploader(token)` → `postShareTokenImage` (`packages/frontend/src/api/images.ts:57`) issues `POST ${BACKEND_BASE}/api/v1/shared/images?token=<share token>`. The share token is an access-granting bearer credential (it mints a Yorkie token and authorizes anonymous writes), and the repo explicitly rejected this placement elsewhere: `packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:75-84` says the share endpoint "Uses POST with the share token in the body so the (access-granting) token stays out of request URLs and access logs." Query strings land in reverse-proxy/CDN access logs, browser history and `Referer` on any cross-origin subresource. Pre-existing for the docs share surface; this change routes the notes share surface through the same path, widening the exposure. Moving the token to a header or body would close it.

samples.summary: Shadow-mode log now interpolates client-influenced document keys/verbs into a log line (log-forging / CWE-117 surface)
samples.evidence: Line 156-161 builds `target` from `body.attributes[].key` and `.verb` and concatenates it into a single-line warning alongside `method`, `status` and `reason`. The attribute key is ultimately the doc key the *client* chose when attaching, so its content is attacker-influenced (the HMAC guard proves only that Yorkie relayed it, not that the value is trusted). Yorkie's own doc-key charset restrictions make a CR/LF injection unlikely, which is why this is minor rather than major — but nothing in this controller validates or escapes the value before logging it, and `parseYorkieDocKey` runs later and independently. If a key can carry a newline, a viewer can forge fake `[shadow] would deny` lines and hide the real one, which is precisely the signal this change was added to make trustworthy. Note the token itself is correctly kept out of the line.

samples.summary: The frontend half of the read-only store guard (`readOnly ? readOnlyNoteStore(raw) : raw`) has no test anywhere
samples.evidence: `notes-view.tsx:152` is the mount-level application of the write guard, and it is the one that decides what the *component* retains (`storeRef`). There is no `notes-view` test file (`packages/frontend/src/app/notes/` has only `notes-undo-integration`, `notes-toolbar`, `yorkie-note-store`, `notes-thumbnail` tests), and the new `shared-notes-layout.test.tsx` mocks `@/app/notes/notes-view` away entirely (line 92), so nothing asserts that a viewer mount is handed a neutered store from the frontend side. The engine-side wrap (`editor.ts:249`) is covered by `packages/notes/src/view/editor.test.ts`, so the guarantee currently rests on the engine remembering — the redundancy the comment claims is untested. A regression that flipped the ternary would be caught by no lane.

samples.summary: `readOnly` is derived by an equality test against "viewer", so any unexpected role value yields a writable mount (fail-open direction)
samples.evidence: `const readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer";` with `ResolvedShareLink.role` typed as bare `string` (`packages/frontend/src/api/share-links.ts:8,17`). An allowlist (`role === "editor"` → writable) would fail closed instead. Impact today is bounded: `ShareLinkService.create` validates against `SHARE_LINK_ROLES` ('viewer'|'editor') before persisting (`share-link.service.ts:77`), and the server-side `hasAccess` fails closed on write, so a third role value is not currently producible. Relocated from `shared-document.tsx` by this change rather than introduced by it; noting it because the same inverted test now also governs whether the token-scoped uploader is handed out (line 74).

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo: the sole server-side gate refusing a share-link viewer's write (`hasAccess` -> `needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true`, yorkie-auth.controller.ts:262) is discarded whenever `this.enforce` is false (constructor :115-116), which is the default — the shadow branch at :149-164 returns HTTP 200 with `{allowed:true, reason:'shadow'}` for any computed deny. No non-test, non-doc location in the repo sets YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE (only test harness revision-history.e2e-spec.ts:292 and template-tier checks register-templates.ts:154 / template-review.ts:80 / template.service.ts:470), and self-hosting.md:185 plus docs/design/sharing.md:208-219 confirm shadow/allow-everything is the stock posture. The exploit chain is reachable: POST /auth/yorkie-token/share (auth.controller.ts:82-90) is public and mints a Yorkie token for any valid share token regardless of role, and the project public key ships in the client bundle (shared-document.tsx:703,957; .env.production.example:59), so a non-frontend Yorkie client can attach to the doc key and write. Client-side read-only mounts (docs/src/store/read-only.ts:40, notes/src/store/read-only.ts:64) bound only this app, not arbitrary clients. This is a fail-open authorization gate squarely in the Security lane; it being deliberate/pre-existing rollout behaviour is not a refutation ground under the instructions.

finding.summary: Share-link `viewer` write authorization is still off by default (shadow mode allow-all); the branch's own docs state a viewer link is write-capable on a stock deployment
finding.evidence: `handleAuth` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:149-164) computes a deny (`hasAccess` → `link.role === 'editor'` for a `rw` verb, line 262) and then returns `{allowed:true}` with HTTP 200 whenever `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE !== 'true'` (line 116). Nothing in the repo sets that variable: I grepped every yml/yaml/env/json/sh and found no deployment config, and there is no code that registers the webhook methods on the Yorkie project either (no `authWebhookMethods` anywhere). Attack: hold any viewer-role share link → `POST /auth/yorkie-token/share` (auth.controller.ts:82-90, public, no session needed) mints a Yorkie token wrapping the share token → attach with a bare `@yorkie-js/sdk` client using `VITE_YORKIE_PUBLIC_KEY`, which ships in every visitor's bundle (shared-document.tsx:957) → PushPull writes to `note-<id>` are allowed because the only gate that would refuse them is bypassed at line 149. This change is the one that expands the share surface (toolbar + `shareTokenImageUploader` on the notes route) while the enforced path stays disabled, and the new docs (docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md Risks, packages/backend/README.md, packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:57-67) explicitly acknowledge it. Pre-existing and deliberate as a staged rollout — but the effective default posture is an authorization bypass for anonymous viewer links, and the only mitigation added here is a boot-time log line.

verdict.reason: The described bypass is present and reachable exactly as claimed. yorkie-auth.controller.ts:115-116 enables enforcement only when YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE==='true'; handleAuth:149-164 throws away any deny decision and answers HTTP 200 {allowed:true} otherwise. The discarded deny is the sole server-side viewer-write gate (hasAccess:262 `needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true`, reached for verb 'rw' via checkAttribute:226). No config in the tree sets the flag to 'true' — only test harnesses (revision-history.e2e-spec.ts:292, yorkie-auth.controller.spec.ts:55) and unrelated template-tier assertions (register-templates.ts:154, template.service.ts:470). Both halves of the exploit chain are public: POST /auth/yorkie-token/share (auth.controller.ts:82-90) has no JwtAuthGuard and mints a Yorkie token wrapping any share token regardless of role, and VITE_YORKIE_PUBLIC_KEY ships in the client bundle (shared-document.tsx:703,957; PrivateRoute.tsx:25). The controller's own comment (86-99) and logPosture warning (132-139) concede that a viewer can write by attaching with their own client and that the read-only mounts bound only this app. In-lane for Security (authorization gate not on the enforced path); pre-existing/deliberate rollout is not a refutation ground I may apply, and no guard elsewhere makes the shadow branch unreachable.

finding.summary: The viewer read-only guarantee this change builds on has no server-side enforcement in the default configuration — the Yorkie auth webhook ships in shadow (allow-all) mode, so every gate added here is client-side only
finding.evidence: `this.enforce = configService.get('YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE') === 'true'` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:101) defaults to false, and lines 111-119 then return ALLOW for a computed deny. `hasAccess()` would otherwise be the only thing refusing `link.role === 'viewer'` a write (line 217). Attack: a holder of a viewer-role share link calls `fetchYorkieShareToken(token)` (the frontend already does this at shared-document.tsx:959 and hands the result to the SDK), attaches with any Yorkie client outside the browser UI, and pushes arbitrary text ops to the note — no client-side `changeFilter`, `EditorState.readOnly` or `runHistory` guard is in the path. The diff's own comments (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:435-437, docs/design/notes/notes.md) acknowledge this, which makes it a known rollout state rather than a regression — but this change materially widens the surface that depends on it (a viewer is now given a live editor pane and the full `NoteEditorAPI` via the mounted toolbar), so it is worth restating that the boundary is unenforced by default. Mitigation is deployment-level (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true`), not code.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. `this.enforce` defaults to false when YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE is unset (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:115-116), and the shadow-mode branch converts a computed deny into HTTP 200 / allowed:true (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:149-164). The viewer write refusal at hasAccess (`needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true`, line 262) is therefore inert in the default configuration, and it is the only server-side place link.role gates a CRDT write. The vector is fully reachable: POST /auth/yorkie-token/share (auth.controller.ts:82-90) is public, unauthenticated, and mints a Yorkie token from any share token with no role check — its own comment delegates role validation to the webhook that is not enforcing. A viewer-link holder can attach with any Yorkie client outside the browser and write. Only the cited line numbers were slightly off (101 vs 115, 111-119 vs 149-164, 217 vs 262); the substance is accurate. No guard elsewhere closes it: the only runtime assertions of the enforce flag are in the template package (register-templates.ts:154, template-review.ts:80, template.service.ts:470), not on the share-link/notes path. The boot-time warning in logPosture (lines 127-140) documents the exposure but does not remove it, and this is squarely in the authorization/access-control lane, so out-of-scope does not apply.
